slide.title: Check, Fix, Explain
slide.body: Left: a video frame with a teal tick. Right: a half-page note with four short lines. Small tag: AI Video Production and Motion · Lesson 14.

scenes.voiceover: You have a script, a shot list, clips, an avatar, an edit, sound, two exports and a checklist. The last step is not about adding more. It is about checking carefully, fixing what matters, and explaining how you made it.

slide.title: Capstone: Finishing and Presenting Your Video
slide.body: AI Video Production and Motion · Lesson 14 of 14 · Capstone step 4

scenes.voiceover: In the last lesson, you completed your pre-publish checklist. This is the final lesson, and capstone step four.

slide.title: The capstone brief
slide.body: "A 60 to 90 second AI-assisted brand or explainer video, from script to final export, plus a half-page production note: tools, key prompts, pre-publish checks."

scenes.voiceover: Here is the capstone brief. Produce a sixty to ninety second AI-assisted brand or explainer video, from script to final export. Add a half-page production note that lists your tools, key prompts and pre-publish checks. The rubric on the course page shows how it is assessed.

slide.title: Two templates
slide.body: Left: script template with rows Hook · Point 1 · Point 2 · Point 3 · Call to action, and columns Viewer sees / Viewer hears. Right: shot-list template with columns #, Time, Dur., Shot type, Camera movement, Viewer sees, Narration, Source, Status.

scenes.voiceover: If you want to rebuild or check your plan, the lesson page has two templates. A two-column script template, and a shot-list template with a status column. The status is keep, trim, regenerate or replace, as in lesson ten.

slide.title: Final pass: four viewings
slide.body: 1. Artifacts: hands, faces, melting, flicker, text, physics (L10) · 2. Continuity: characters, clothes, colours, settings (L08)

scenes.voiceover: Now the final quality pass. Watch the whole video four times, each time for one thing. First, artifacts, like hands, faces, melting objects and flicker. Second, continuity of characters, clothes, colours and settings.

slide.title: Final pass, continued
slide.body: 3. Audio: every word clear on phone speakers (L12) · 4. Captions: correct, inside the safe area (L11, L12). Then: fix the most visible problems, export 16:9 and 9:16.

scenes.voiceover: Third, audio. Every word must be clear over the music, on phone speakers. Fourth, captions. Every line must be correct and inside the safe area. Fix the most visible problems first. Then do the final export of both versions.

slide.title: The production note
slide.body: 1. Tools and what each did · 2. Two or three key prompts, exactly · 3. Problems and how you solved them · 4. Pre-publish checks

scenes.voiceover: Then write the production note. Half a page, with four parts. The tools you used and what each did. Two or three key prompts, shown exactly. The main problems and how you solved them. And your pre-publish checks.

scenes.stock_query: engineer writing notes beside finished machine
scenes.voiceover: The production note is like the notes an engineer leaves with a finished machine. Someone else, or you in six months, can see what was used, how it was built and what was checked.

scenes.stock_query: woman riding bicycle along seaside road
scenes.voiceover: Let's see an example. Lan is a content creator in Da Nang, Vietnam. Her capstone is a seventy-two second explainer for a bicycle-rental app. The app is made up for this lesson.

slide.title: Lan's final pass, part 1
slide.body: Shot 7: wheel bends for half a second → Trim. Shots 4–5: helmet white, then grey → Replace shot 5 with a close-up of the phone screen.

scenes.voiceover: In her final pass, she finds four problems. A wheel bends for half a second in shot seven, so she trims it. The rider's helmet changes from white to grey between shots four and five, so she replaces shot five with a close-up of the phone screen.

slide.title: Lan's final pass, part 2
slide.body: Call to action: music too loud → Lower it. Caption 'Da / Nang' split over two lines → Edit onto one line.

scenes.voiceover: The music is too loud under the call to action, so she lowers it. And the caption Da Nang is split badly over two lines, so she edits it.

scenes.broll_prompt: A young Vietnamese woman in a white helmet rides a blue bicycle along a seaside road; medium shot; slow tracking shot beside her; bright morning sun with soft shadows; clean modern commercial style, natural colours; 6 seconds; no readable text, no brand names, no logos.
scenes.voiceover: Here is one of her shots. A young woman in a white helmet rides a blue bicycle along a seaside road, with a slow tracking shot beside her.

slide.title: Production note: tools
slide.body: Flow: 4 text-to-video shots · Kling: 3 image-to-video shots from keyframes · HeyGen: stock avatar, 15-second intro · CapCut: edit, captions, export

scenes.voiceover: Now her production note. Her tools were Flow for four text-to-video shots, Kling for three image-to-video shots from keyframes, a HeyGen stock avatar for the intro, and CapCut for the edit, captions and export.

slide.title: Key prompt and checks
slide.body: Lan's key prompt from content.md word for word: 'A young woman in a white helmet rides a blue rental bicycle along a seaside road. Medium shot. Slow tracking shot beside her. Bright morning sun, soft shadows. Clean modern commercial style. 6 seconds.' Below: Problems solved: helmet drift, hands artifact. Checks: AI disclosure · stock avatar only · no real people · music licence saved · tool terms checked.

scenes.voiceover: She shows her key prompt exactly, as you can see on screen. She explains the problems she solved, like the helmet drift, and a hands artifact she fixed by adding hands on handlebars, steady ride. And she lists her checks. A disclosure line, a stock avatar only, no real people, a saved music licence, and tool terms checked for her plan.

A common mistake is to spend the last hours generating new clips, and then run out of time for the quality pass and the note. A simpler video that is checked and well documented is stronger. Stop generating early.

slide.title: Key takeaways
slide.body: 1. 60–90 second video + half-page production note. 2. Four viewings: artifacts · continuity · audio · captions. 3. Note: tools, prompts, problems, checks.

scenes.voiceover: Let's recap. First, the capstone is a sixty to ninety second video from script to final export, plus a half-page production note. Second, do the final quality pass in four viewings: artifacts, continuity, audio and captions. Third, the note lists your tools, key prompts, problems solved and checks.

Congratulations. You have gone from an idea to a finished video, and you directed every step. Now complete capstone step four. Do your final pass, export both versions, and write your production note. It takes about forty-five minutes. Then submit your video, the note, your shot list and your checklist. Well done, and good luck with your capstone.
